payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
node.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the hand holding the paper over the cup; the paper is visibly outside the cup, not stuffed inside it.

s3: The node’s binding already correctly distinguishes object correspondence from mere proximity and reserves unknown for genuine ambiguity. The traces repeatedly identify a hand-held paper-like object in front of a round object, but cannot match either to the source paper and cup; the images support that caution, so do not force “no” from the reference label or treat parent fail observations as proof of correspondence. However, the binding’s ellipsis/underspecification may leave the decision criterion too open: make the typed pass/fail/unknown rules explicit and require evidence for both correspondence and the paper’s spatial relation before judging progress. In particular, distinguish a clearly identifiable pair with no movement toward insertion (fail) from an unmatchable pair (unknown); do not equate “not fully stuffed” or mere holding/overlap with progress. The repeated high-confidence unknowns suggest the criterion is being applied consistently, not that confidence should be lowered. There are no transport, schema, or dependency failures to address; the unresolved outcome is visual correspondence ambiguity, and the aggregate reference label alone does not resolve it.

The edited image shows a hand-held printed sheet and a partly occluded round object, while the source shows a white sheet and blue cup; the traces do not establish that these are the same objects. Do not infer correspondence or force the reference “no” label. Repeated high-confidence unresolved outputs indicate a criterion/binding issue, not a need to lower confidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported."}
